x: Our first man home was that old warrior Bert Footer and next came Geoff Pearson, whom we do not see very much these days. Dick Towndrow and George Chantler both retired and this left our "A" team with only two finishers.

Les Stokell won the individual race with Syd Ring third and Bert Footer fourth. Bert was running for our “ B ” team, otherwise we should have scored a hollow win in the team race but even so we still came out winners and Syd Ring also took 2nd prize in the individual handicap race.

Carter, Footer, Penny, Herbert, Green, Scrimshaw, Lucas and Stimpson were no more endowed than some of our present men; they merely exploited their gifts more by plenty of hard training and by turning out regularly in all Club matches.
Under the stern leadership of Footer, Carter and Penny in the immediate post-war years, Mac soon showed he was possessed of great endurance and performed well over the road and country.
The winner on this occasion-Les Cohen, followed by Footer, Jack Flower, Duffett, Penny, Allum, Rice, Pyer, with, needless to say, a Belgrave team win of convincing proportions.

Penny, Carter, Allum and Footer also in their time contended with this "natural obstacle", but the retention of this section of the course can only be prompted nowadays in the cause of sentimentality or tradition or pure sadism - (blow you Jack, I have my Wellington boots on) - I am also fully aware…

Macdonald and Footer couldn't have supplied enough superlatives to sum up my feelings. Each stride felt as though it would be my last, I resolved this would be my final road race, wished I had never been a runner and cursed myself for ever getting into the team.
Our scorers were Penny (3rd), Duffett(4th), Mitchell (5th), Cook (7th), Footer (9th) and Rice (15th). South London Harriers (120) were second and Mitcham A.C.
